<description>
{
 "summary": "Adds several systemd sandboxing directives to contrib/init/bitcoind.service, including kernel tunables/logs/modules protection, clock and hostname restrictions, proc visibility controls, namespace restrictions, and an empty capability bounding set. It also restricts socket address families to AF_INET, AF_INET6, AF_UNIX, and AF_NETLINK, applies system call filtering, and updates the ExecStartPre chgrp prefix modifier from ! to + so pre-exec operations retain required privileges under the new capability limits.",
 "problem": "Linux systems deploying bitcoind using the contrib systemd service file lack defense-in-depth isolation, granting the daemon access to kernel tunables, clock settings, unneeded namespaces, and unconstrained syscalls that are unnecessary for normal operation.",
 "evidence": [
  "PR description: 'Adds sandboxing options that `bitcoind` doesn't need to be exempt from... Also switches the `ExecStartPre` `chgrp` from \"!\" to \"+\", since \"!\" only lifts `User=`/`Group=`, and the new syscall filter and capability bounding set would block it otherwise.'"
 ],

<category name="tools" title="Tools and scripts">
## Covers

Command-line tools other than the node and its RPC client, and the
scripts under contrib: `bitcoin-tx`, `bitcoin-util`, the offline
`bitcoin-wallet` tool, the `bitcoin` wrapper, seed and asmap
generation, signet tooling, tracing scripts, and developer helper
scripts. Build and release scripts are build; test helpers are tests.
The Scripts and tools label is a strong prior.

## What matters here

Tools that operators and downstream projects depend on first: seed
generation, asmap, signet, and the wallet tool affect real deployments.
Then correctness of any tool that touches keys or transactions. Then
developer productivity tools that many contributors use. Then niche or
single-user scripts, which rank low regardless of size.
